column2: Friends, praise no other; do not wish harm. Praise Indra the bull together at the pressing, and recite the hymns again and again.
No work of him who has made the ever-growing one perishes; by sacrifices praise Indra, the all-praised, skilful, unassailable, bold in strength.
He who, without any support, breaks things before the collar-bones, the bounteous, rich in wealth, joins what is joined and restores again what is broken.
May a thousand, a hundred, yoked to your golden chariot, your prayer-yoked, long-maned bay horses carry you, Indra, to drink the soma.
Come, Indra, with your joyful bay horses, with peacock-feathered coats; let none, though they bind you, hold you back; pass beyond them like an archer.
You indeed, O mightiest god, are praised for the mortal; there is no other than you, bounteous one, to be gracious; Indra, I speak this word to you.
You, Indra, are glorious, the receiver of the pressed soma, lord of strength; you alone slay the unopposed Vritras, the supporter of peoples, urged on by many.
We call on Indra for worship; Indra at the progressing sacrifice; Indra in battle, we the singers call, and Indra for the winning of wealth.
May these songs of mine strengthen you, O rich in wealth; the pure, fire-colored sages have sung to you with hymns.
These sweetest songs and hymns of praise rise up — they are victory-winning, wealth-giving, unfailing helpers, striving like chariots.
As a thirsty wild buffalo goes to the prepared water, so come swiftly in our kinship and our approach; drink well among the Kanvas.
Be able, lord of power, Indra, with all your helps; for we follow you, O hero, as fortune, glorious, finder of wealth.
The arms, Indra, that you brought from the Asuras, winning the light — increase, bounteous one, this singer and those who have spread the grass for you.
Sing forth a praise-song, fitting, to Mitra and Aryaman, O keepers of truth; sing the hymn to Varuna, the protector, among the kings.
The Ayus, with hymns, for your first drinking, O Indra; the Ribhus joined in one voice; the Rudras praised the ancient one.
O Maruts, offer the prayer for your great Indra; the Vritra-slayer, hundred-powered, slays Vritra with the hundred-jointed thunderbolt.
Sing the great song to Indra, O Maruts, the best slayer of Vritra, by which the truth-strengtheners brought forth light — a wakeful god for the god.
O Indra, bring us wisdom, as a father to his sons; teach us in this course, O much-invoked, that living we may attain the light.
Indra, do not abandon us; be with us in the shared feast; you are our help, you our kinship; Indra, do not forsake us.
We who have pressed the soma for you, Vritra-slayer, and spread the grass, sit around the streams of the filter, as the waters.
Indra, the strength and manly power that you have among the Nahusha peoples, or among the five tribes — bring that splendor, and all manly powers together.
Truly, thus you are a bull; our helper is urged on by bulls; you, fierce one, are heard far away; the bull is renowned near and far.
Whether, mighty one, you are far away, or nearby, Vritra-slayer, from there the pressed-soma giver, with his bay horses, honors you with songs.
In the delights of the drink, sing with song for yourselves the great, wise hero Indra, the powerful, of famed name, in words.
Indra, grant a threefold refuge, threefold shelter, for welfare; give protection to the bountiful and to me; drive away from these the shining enemies.
They seek the sun as if resting; enjoy all that belongs to Indra; born, the born wins wealth by might; we shine to claim our share.
No mortal of long life, not divine, attains that food; even Etasha yoked, Indra yokes his bay horses.
Honor Indra, to be called in all battles; come to our prayers and soothing offerings, Vritra-slayer, with highest verses.
Yours alone, Indra, is the lowest wealth; you nourish the middle; you rule completely over all, the highest too; none hinders you among the cattle.
Where do you go, where are you? Your mind is in many places. O warrior, fort-destroyer, the Gayatri songs have been sung.
We have indeed fed this thunderbolt-bearer here; today at the pressing bring the soma for him; honor now the famed one.
The king of the peoples, who goes in chariots, irresistible, conqueror of all armies, the foremost Vritra-slayer — I praise him.
From whatever we fear, Indra, make us safe from that; bounteous one, help us for our protection; drive away foes and enemies.
O lord of the dwelling, firm pillar, assembly of the soma-drinkers; the drop, breaker of the eternal forts, Indra, friend of sages.
Indeed you are great, O Sun; indeed, O Aditya, you are great; the greatness of you who exist is most to be praised; by might, O god, you are great.
The friend of yours, Indra, who has a horse, a chariot, a fair form and cattle, is always accompanied with vigor and wealth and goes to the assembly with shining gifts.
Though a hundred heavens and a hundred earths were yours, Indra, a thousand suns would not equal you, O thunderbolt-bearer; the two worlds do not encompass you at birth.
Indra, when you are called by men from east, west, north and west, from many places — you are the mighty protector of Anu, Turvasha, praised for strength.
What mortal, O Indra, dares to withstand you, Vasu? For faith in you, bounteous one, in the farther heaven, the strong man wins strength.
Indra and Agni: this footless one came first of the footed; leaving her head, she chattered with her tongue, and the thirty-footed one stepped on.
Indra, come very near with your helps of measured wisdom; come with the most auspicious, with blessings, with good friends.
From here your help, unaging, the sender, the unsent; swift, victorious, the chariot-warrior, unconquered, who strengthens Tugrya.
Let not the ritual priests keep you from us far away; come to our shared feast from near or far, and listen here.
Press soma for the soma-drinker, Indra the thunderbolt-bearer; cook the cakes for his help; the giver gives joy to the giver.
We call on Indra, who is a conqueror in battle and all-seeing, of a thousand moods, of much strength, lord of the good; be present in battles to help us grow.
O you of power and wealth, with your powers show us the way by day and night; may your gift never fail, nor ours to you.
Whenever the mortal praiser grows old before the generous one, let him then worship Varuna, upholder of the sacred laws, with a wise song.
Protect our cattle in the exhilaration of the drink, for Indra, O Medhyatithi — who is mingled with the two bay horses, who is golden, Indra the thunderbolt-bearer, golden.
Let Indra hear both of ours, this word of ours here; the strongest, bounteous one comes with thought, together, to drink the soma.
O stone-bearer, you are not given away for a great price; not for a thousand, nor ten thousand, nor a hundred, O lord of a hundred.
Indra, you are better to me than a father and a brother who does not share; you and my mother both shelter me, O Vasu, for wealth and bounty.
These soma-drinks are pressed for Indra, mixed with curds; come to them, thunderbolt-handed, with your bay horses, to drink and be glad.
These soma-drinks, Indra, are for your delight, to be praised; having drunk the honey, hear our songs; give to the praiser, O lover of songs.
Today I invoke you, Indra, the milch cow with Gayatri-shaped body, the good milker, and other nourishment, wide-streaming and well adorned.
Neither the great stones nor the obstacles can hold you back, Indra, when you give wealth to the praiser like me; no one ever diminishes you.
Who knows him, drinking with us at the pressing? What strength has he won? He who, delighted by the soma-drink of the fair-jawed, breaks the forts with might.
Indra, when you drive out the lawless from the assembly, uplift our desirable soma-stalk and exalt it in wealth.
May Tvashtar, Parjanya, Brahmanaspati and Aditi with sons and brothers protect us by a divine, hard-to-resist saving word.
You never overthrow, Indra; you do not cling to the giver; come ever nearer, bounteous one; the gift of the god is increasing in abundance.
Yoke your two bay horses, O best Vritra-slayer, from far away; come near, bounteous one, fierce, with the bright ones, to drink the soma.
Men, the nourishing, swelled you yesterday, thunderbolt-bearer; you, O Indra, bearer of hymns, hear here and come to the dwelling.
The daughter of heaven, coming forth, has been seen, shining; the great one uncovers the waters; with her eye she makes the darkness into light, O fair one.
These cows of the dawn call you, O Ashvins, to heaven's sacrifice; I call you here for help, O you of power and wealth, for you go to every clan.
Where, O Ashvins, is the mortal who does you honor? Strike with the stone; the pressed soma-juice, the stalk, as in a mortar.
Here is your sweetest pressed soma, Ashvins, at the heavenly sacrifices; drink it across the day; bestow jewels on the giver.
Always begging, I approach you with a cup of soma; who has not begged the ruler who is enraged at the pressings like a wild beast?
O Adhvaryu, hasten the soma; Indra is thirsty; he has just yoked his two bay stallions and the Vritra-slayer has come.
Then bring, Indra, the greater than the lesser; for you, bounteous, have become the wealthy and are to be invoked in every battle.
Indra, as much as you are, I would be master of so much; I would nourish your praiser, O giver of wealth, and I would not exult in evil.
You, Indra, overcome all rivals in conflicts; you are the destroyer of slander, a begetter, the Vritra-smiter; you hasten the straining.
You who by might surpass the seat of heaven; no earthly space contains you, Indra; you have borne beyond all.
The god-pleasing juice, mixed with milk, has been pressed; Indra has spoken among the born; we wake you, O bay-horsed one, with sacrifices; wake our song in the joy of the drink.
Your seat, Indra, has been made in the house; come with the men, O much-invoked; be our helper, a strengthener, give treasures, and rejoice in the soma.
You split the cavities, you released the streams; you gave rest to the confined seas; great Indra, when you released the mountain and struck down the Danavas, the streams flowed.
We, pressing, praise you, Indra, of great strength, seeking strength; bring us good fortune whose end we may reach, protected by you.
We have grasped your right hand, Indra, desiring wealth, O lord of wealth; we know you, O hero, lord of cattle; give us shining, bounteous wealth.
Men call on Indra, the near friend, when the thoughts yoke to cross; the hero, winner of men, the desire of fame — share with us a cattle-stocked pen.
The birds, the fair-winged, the sages of dear wisdom, sat near Indra, begging; drive away the darkness, fill the eye, free us who are bound as with a snare.
When they saw you flying in the sky as a fair-winged bird, longing, with the heart; golden-winged, Varuna's messenger, a bird nourishing in Yama's seat.
The first Brahman born, in the beginning, the shining Vena uncovered the borders; he opened the depths, the nearest places, the womb of being and non-being.
Unprecedented, the best have been made for this great, brave, strong, swift one; they fashioned most gracious words for this loud thunderbolt-bearer, the ancient.
The dark drop descended into the stream of the Amshumati with ten thousand; Indra with his power found it blowing; the man-minded drove off the enemy.
Driven by the breath of Vritra, all the gods who were friends abandoned you; Indra, may friendship with the Maruts be yours; then you shall conquer all these armies.
The gray one swallowed the shaker, the youth, in the gathering of many; see the poem of the god in its greatness — today he is dead, yesterday he lived.
You, O Indra, born, were a foe to the seven without foes; you found heaven and earth hidden, you set joy in the pervading worlds.

We praise you, thunderbolt-bearer, like a ram-leader, strong-toothed, full of power, bull, firm; you make the foes of the strong flow, desiring their service; I praise Indra the sky-dweller, the Vritra-slayer.
Bring your offering to the great, who grows by greatness; make favor to the wise one; roam through the ancient clans, fulfilling the peoples.
We invoke Indra, the bounteous, the best of men in this contest for the winning of strength; he hears, the fierce one, for help, slaying Vritras in battles, winning wealth.
Raise up the prayers, O Vasishtha, for fame; honor Indra in the battle; he who extended all by his glory, who hears my words in distress.
The wheel of his that sat in the waters — then that sweetness covered it for him; the udder that is spread over the earth — you placed milk in the cows and in the plants.
We call here for welfare on that strong Tarkshya, urged by the gods, the vigorous, the overcomer of chariots — of unharmed felly, swift, the winner of armies.
Savior Indra, helper Indra, at every call easy to call, Indra the hero; I call Shakra, the much-invoked Indra; may the bounteous Indra enjoy this offering.
We worship Indra, thunderbolt in his right hand, charioteer of the bay horses of the different courses; with his beard shaking, standing high, he overcomes fear with armies and wealth.
We praise Indra, the conqueror, the bold, the driver, great, boundless, bull, with the good thunderbolt; the slayer of Vritra, winner of strength, giver of gifts, the bounteous, the generous.
The mortal who would harm us, or considers himself strong, or swift, destroy him in battle or by strength; may we, urged by you, Indra, overcome him with manly spirit.
He whom the peoples, contending in the Vritra-fights, call on, whom the speeding call when yoked, in the winning of heroes, in the lap of the waters, whom the sages invigorate — he is Indra.
O Indra and Parvata, bring with your great chariot the desirable nourishments with fair heroes; enjoy the offerings at the sacrifices, O gods; grow strong with songs and Ida, rejoicing.
For Indra the unsharpened songs were sent forth; he drove the waters from the depth of the sea; he who, as with an axle, supported on all sides the earth and heaven with his powers.
Friends have turned you toward friendship, having crossed many seas; the ordainer has set the grandson of the father in this dwelling, shining the more.
Who today yokes to the pole the cows of truth, the shining, the hard-to-subdue, the active? Near them are the water-carriers, joyful ones — whoever pays their wage may live.
